Shell_Pest_2025_Clam

2025-10-13

To make things cleaner this is only code for Clam Counts and Prevalence. Polydora and Cliona will be addressed in separate scripts.


~~~ Counts: Initial GLMM Models ~~~

Section -2.943 1.057 2 0.59 0.126 0.126 0.000 
## === Counts: BIAS TESTING IMPORTANCE TABLE & ICC ===
##       1. MASSIVE Adjusted ICC indicates that after controlling for other factors, ~49% of the variance is attributable to the random effect of ProcessedBy and ~27% is attributable to FixedLocation, which is overwhelming.
##       2. The Check for Multicollinearity show that the model’s fixed effects are clean, independent, and interpretable. No red flags for collinearity.
##       3. Large Positive ΔAIC indicates that TotalWeight is an extremely important predictor. 
##       3. Section's negative ΔAIC indicates it doesn't really improve the model.
##       4. TotalWeight has a very small p-values (e-211), indicating it is highly significant.
##       5. Year and Season are both significant with very low p-values (e-15 and e-14).
##       6. Section is not significant (p = 0.59).
##       7. ΔR2 measures how much of the model’s explained variance is uniquely attributable to that predictor. TotalWeight explains ~6% on its own; Year and Season add only ~0.5% and 0.4%, respectively; Section contributes virtually nothing.
##  |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| CONCLUSION |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| 
##     1. TotalWeight is by far the strongest driver of clam counts. Heavier oysters tend to have more clams.
##     2. Given the outsized impact of bias on this data, no other strong insights can be drawn without significant reprocessing, retraining, and robust QA measures being put in place. After which all these tests need to be run again and more detailed analysis run to determine any significant differences.
##     3. This solution represents a large input of staff time (thousands of hours) for a small amount of benefit.
## *** 4. Recommendation is to discontinue counting clams in ShellPest data. ***

##       1. Model fits the data pretty well with good residuals and and R-squared MASSIVELY better than the Improved model. KS Test fail is expected with a large data set, and nothing looks wrong with the plot otherwise.
##       2. ACF series residuals series exhibit no significant autocorrelation, implying that the model has effectively captured the temporal dependencies.
##       3. The MASSIVE increase in model performance with both biases raise a lot of doubt about the Improved Model's insights.

## === Prevalence: BIAS TESTING IMPORTANCE TABLE & ICC ===
##       1. Adjusted ICC indicates that after controling for other factors, ~25% of the variance is attributable to the random effect of ProcessedBy and 5% to FixedLocation, which is a good amount
##       2. The Check for Multicollinearity show that the model’s fixed effects are clean, independent, and interpretable. No red flags for collinearity.
##       3. Large Positive ΔAIC indicates that TotalWeight and Processed by are extremely important predictors. 
##       4. Section and ShellHeight's negative ΔAIC indicates they doesn't really improve the model.
##       5. TotalWeight have very small p-values indicating it is highly significant.
##       6. Year and Season are both significant with very low p-values, but far less than weight.
##       7. ShellHeight and Section are not significant (p = 0.32 and p = 0.64).
##       8. ΔR2 measures how much of the model’s explained variance is uniquely attributable to that predictor. TotalWeight explains ~2.5% on its own; Year and Season add less than 1% each; ShellHeight and Section contribute virtually nothing.
##  |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| CONCLUSION |||||||||||||||||||||||||||| 
##     1. TotalWeight is by far the strongest driver of clam prevalence. Heavier oysters tend to have more clams.
##     2. Given the outsized impact of bias on this data, no other strong insights can be drawn without significant reprocessing, retraining, and robust QA measures being put in place. After which all these tests need to be run again and more detailed analysis run to determine any significant differences.
##     3. This solution represents a large input of staff time (thousands of hours) for a small amount of benefit.
## *** 4. Recommendation is to discontinue noting the presence or absence of clams in ShellPest data. ***
